text: Before anyone tunes anything, Brennan needs a real reference point. This video plans the performance baseline for BrennanERP, captured before the AG exists and again right after it goes live.
Two things get captured: wait statistics showing what BrennanERP spends its time waiting on, and a Query Store baseline of the top CPU, duration, and read-heavy queries -- both taken twice, not once.
The key comparison: the post-cutover run should show a new HADR_SYNC_COMMIT wait. Not a bug to chase -- the real, measured cost of synchronous-commit, written down instead of assumed.

Standing monitoring sits on top: Agent job failures alerting same-day, AG health checked against sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states, and disk/CPU thresholds watched on both nodes -- not a one-time exercise.
The baseline and the watch are both planned. Next: the first lesson that actually builds something -- the Windows Server Failover Cluster itself.
